$description: Hubtask Design System — Foundations v0.1. W3C DTCG format. This file is the single source of truth for every colour, spacing, radius, duration and easing value in the product. CSS custom properties, typed TypeScript constants and the Go label-token name list are all generated from it. Never write these values anywhere else. Set 'primitive' holds raw values; sets 'semantic.light' and 'semantic.dark' hold the two theme modes; 'motion' names what a movement is for, 'density' how much air a region carries and 'layout' the measures of the shell. Application code binds to 'semantic', 'motion', 'density' and 'layout', never to 'primitive'.

indigo.$description: The primary hue: the main action, selection, the focus ring and the brand text (design-system.md §1).

raspberry.$description: The signature hue. Signature colour only - deliberately carries no system meaning; danger has its own red.

danger.$description: A vivid red of its own, warmer than the signature raspberry so that an alarm and the brand are told apart by hue as well as by the icon a status always carries.

violet.$description: The AI tint: a proposal, never the reader's own content.

neutral.$description: Cool neutrals, tinted toward the primary hue. The light canvas, the dark canvas, surface and raised are the steps design-system.md §6 rule 1 names.

borderWidth.$description: Border widths. A hairline round a control is the one measurement wave 1 needs that the radius and space scales do not carry, and `lint-no-literals` catches it at the first Checkbox - which is what makes this a scale rather than a preference. Three steps and no more: `hairline` draws a boundary, `thick` draws one that has to be seen at a glance, and `ring` is rule 5's focus ring and nothing else.

hairline.$description: The boundary of a control, and the divider between two of them.

thick.$description: A boundary that carries state: a checked box, a selected card.

ring.$description: Rule 5's focus ring, at rule 5's offset. Never a border.

layer.$description: The layering scale. Every element that leaves the flow takes its z-index from here and never from a number written at the call site - five overlays each picking their own is the failure design-system.md avoids by having this scale at all. The steps are ten apart so that a component may sit one above its own layer without borrowing the next one's rank.

base.$description: The document flow. Nothing is raised.

raised.$description: Lifted within the flow: a card under the pointer, a row being dragged.

sticky.$description: Stays put while the page scrolls under it: the app bar, a table header.

overlay.$description: The scrim, and what is anchored to the viewport edge behind a dialog: a drawer.

dialog.$description: A modal that owns the focus until it is dismissed.

popover.$description: Anchored to a trigger and dismissed by it: Menu, Popover, a Select list. Above a dialog, because one opens inside one.

tooltip.$description: Transient, never focusable, and above the control it describes wherever that control sits.

toast.$description: Says something happened. Nothing may cover it, so nothing is above it.

dwell.$description: How long a passing message stays before it leaves on its own: a toast's confirmation. Not a movement - nothing animates over it - but a time a reader is given to read one short sentence. It never runs out while the pointer is over the message or focus is in it (WCAG 2.2.1); that is the frame's rule, this is only its length.

dwell-offering.$description: How long a passing message that offers something - Undo, an action - stays: long enough to read it, decide and reach the control by keyboard, which a plain confirmation does not ask for. Never shorter than `dwell`.

linear.$description: No acceleration. What a continuous indicator turns at - a loop that eased would appear to stall twice a revolution.

large.$description: Desktop, detail pane on the right

motion.$description: What a movement is for (design-system.md §6 rule 6). Easings and durations alone do not say which is entrance, which is exit, which is emphasis and which carries a celebration slot - and components that each choose disagree about how long an entrance lasts. A component names the role; the pair behind it is decided here, once. Rule 6 still applies on top: every one of these reduces to the colour change under reduced motion, and none of them animates anything but opacity and transform.

state.$description: A control acknowledging a change to itself - checked, switched, pressed, hovered. The reader is looking straight at it and is waiting for nothing, so it is the shortest role there is.

pending.$description: A continuous indicator: something is happening and nobody knows for how long. The one role with no beginning and no end, which is why it is a role of its own rather than a slow entrance - it never arrives. Its easing is linear because a loop that eased would appear to stall twice a revolution.

attach.$description: A layer arriving against an anchor the reader is already at: a tooltip, a menu, a popover. It is faster than an entrance because the pointer is already there - a delay here reads as lag rather than as arrival.

entrance.$description: A surface arriving on its own, away from the pointer: a dialog, a toast, a drawer. Slower than an attach on purpose - it appears where the reader was not looking, and the movement is what carries their eye to it.

exit.$description: A surface leaving. Always shorter than its arrival: waiting for something that is already finished is the one delay a reader notices every time. Most components leave without an animation - dismissal unmounts the node.

emphasis.$description: Drawing attention to something that is already on screen and has not moved: a row accepting a drop, a value that changed underneath the reader. The spring is what separates it from a state change.

celebration.$description: §7's slot, and nothing else. The one role that may be longer than a fifth of a second, because it is the only movement whose purpose is to be enjoyed rather than understood. The pair below is tier 1 - every completion, the micro-animation on the row - and the two tiers beneath it are longer and still short; `area` and `travel` are §7's other two guardrails, the most a celebration may claim of the screen and the furthest anything in it may move, as dimensions rather than shares because a share of a viewport nobody has measured is not a value a token can carry. Every tier reduces to rule 6's colour change under reduced motion.

tier2.$description: Tier 2, the structural moment: a movement across the parent row. Longer than tier 1, and over before a reader could wait for it.

tier3.$description: Tier 3, the rare one: the moment that may be enjoyed. The longest movement in the product, and still under a second and a half - never blocking, never waited for.

area.$description: The most a celebration's slot may claim along its longer edge. A third of a small laptop's height, and a corner of anything larger: the calm default stays in view.

travel.$description: The furthest anything in a celebration moves. Transform only (rule 6), and short enough that nothing crosses what somebody is reading.

density.$description: How much air a control and a row carry (design-system.md §5): a task tool with long lists needs a density decision beside the size prop. It is a property of the region rather than of the component - a list of two hundred rows does not want each row told individually - so it travels as data-density the way the theme travels as data-theme (ADR-0043), and size stays what it is: how prominent one control is next to another. Unlike the theme, this scale HAS a correct default and the stylesheet gives it one: a document that forgets data-density gets comfortable and looks right, because extra air is not a defect the way the wrong colour scheme is. The floor is not a taste: no min in either mode is below 24px, which is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's minimum target size. A denser step would be a conformance failure rather than a preference.

comfortable.$description: The default, and what wave 1 was built at. The control and row steps are the ones the components already wrote, moved to where a second component cannot disagree with them. One value changes rather than moves: a small Input and Select had 8px of block padding inside a shell declaring a 32px minimum, so the minimum was decorative and the field was taller than it said. It now takes the small step, which is what Button sm already used.

compact.$description: One step tighter, for a screen that is mostly rows. Every control drops to the next step down and sm lands on 24px, which is the floor named above and not a value that may be tuned further - an IconButton is square, so compact sm is exactly a 24x24 target.

spacious.$description: The phone's step (ADR-0061). Below primitive.breakpoint.medium, and wherever the pointer is coarse, the frame sets data-density="spacious": a 48px control and a wider row, which is where the two platform guidelines for touch put the target. It is the third value of the region's property and not a component's concern - a component reads the same custom properties in every mode.

layout.$description: The measures of the shell (ADR-0061), mode-independent like motion: widths and heights as tokens rather than sums of space steps, because a width may not be written at a call site. A component reads them as --layout-*; nothing else declares a width of the shell.

height.$description: The bar at the top, the same height on every width; the safe-area inset is added to it, never written into it.
The destinations on compact, plus the bottom safe-area inset. Taller than a control: a thumb, not a pointer.

width.$description: The entry to search in the bar from medium up: a few words' worth, so that the bar stays a bar.

open.$description: The search in the bar once it is used: as wide as its list, so the words and what they found read at one width.

width.$description: The pinned navigation from expanded up.

rail.$description: The navigation collapsed to its marks.

min.$description: The narrowest a person may drag the pinned navigation: a hub's name and its figure still fit.

max.$description: The widest a person may drag the pinned navigation: past it the column takes the content's room.

width.$description: The detail column from large up - one column of the entry, as on compact.
The entry panel over a list from large up, as it opens before a person drags it: the entry with its details column beside its text.

min.$description: The narrowest a person may drag the entry panel: the entry's head and one column of details still fit.

max.$description: What xlarge caps the content at, as its breakpoint has described since v0.1.

wide.$description: A dialog the person works in rather than answers: capture, with its chips, its field and its modes on one line each.

column.$description: A board column, padding included: as wide as a card wants to be and no wider, so four columns and the next one fit beside the navigation, as the concept draws them. The board scrolls, not the column.

raised.$description: What stands above a bg.surface plane - a menu, a popover, a dialog, a card on its column. In light it equals the surface, white being the ceiling, and elevation.raised carries the depth; in dark it is a step lighter. The steps between canvas, surface and raised are held by the contrast test.

brand.$description: The Hubtask mark's parts (design-system.md §9): the open outline is the hub, the plane the collection, the core the task, the spark the moment of completion. The tile and its outline draw the installed app's icon, one form for both schemes. Never a text colour - that is text.brand.

status.$description: A status as a surface, a border, a text and an accent (ADR-0061 decision 3) - the four roles ai.* established, for the four system meanings and the neutral. Which step of a ramp serves which role is the contrast test's verdict: text on surface 4.5:1, border and accent 3:1 against every surface, text.inverse on accent 4.5:1 for the emphasised form. text.danger, text.success and text.warning resolve to the same primitives as the matching status.*.text and stay for the callers that read them.

glow.$description: The accent's glow, worn only by the one primary action of a page (design-system.md §6 rule 1). Decorative: the focus ring and the fill are measured on the surface beneath it.

ambient.$description: Tint laid over the canvas. Used as the colour stops of the two radial gradients on <body>; the geometry of those gradients is layout and stays in CSS.

raised.$description: What stands above a bg.surface plane - a menu, a popover, a dialog, a card on its column. In light it equals the surface, white being the ceiling, and elevation.raised carries the depth; in dark it is a step lighter. The steps between canvas, surface and raised are held by the contrast test.

brand.$description: The Hubtask mark's parts (design-system.md §9): the open outline is the hub, the plane the collection, the core the task, the spark the moment of completion. The tile and its outline draw the installed app's icon, one form for both schemes. Never a text colour - that is text.brand.

status.$description: The dark surfaces are opaque soft steps of each family, so every text and border is measured on the colour a reader sees on any plane; the border carries the boundary (rule 3).

glow.$description: The accent's glow, worn only by the one primary action of a page (design-system.md §6 rule 1). Decorative: the focus ring and the fill are measured on the surface beneath it.

ambient.$description: Tint laid over the canvas. Used as the colour stops of the two radial gradients on <body>; the geometry of those gradients is layout and stays in CSS.
